draft.title: True bearings
card: A true bearing is an angle measured clockwise from north. It is written with three figures and the letter T, so 45° is written 045°T.
The four main directions are north 000°T, east 090°T, south 180°T and west 270°T. A full turn is 360°, so 360°T points north again, the same direction as 000°T.

A direction halfway between two of these is halfway between their bearings. North-east lies between north (000°T) and east (090°T), so it is 045°T. North-west lies between west (270°T) and north (use 360°T here), so it is 315°T.
The bearing back is half a turn round. If the bearing from A to B is under 180°T, add 180° to get the bearing from B to A. If it is 180°T or more, subtract 180°.
draft.remember: Bearings start at north and turn clockwise, and end with T. The way back is 180° different.

a.why: South-east is halfway between east (090°T) and south (180°T), so it is 135°T. 225°T is tempting, but that is south-west, halfway between south and west.
a.clue: Find the angle halfway between east and south.

b.q: Lena walks from her camp to a lookout on a true bearing of 305°T. What is the true bearing from the lookout back to the camp?
b.why: The bearing is 180°T or more, so subtract 180°: \(305^{\circ} - 180^{\circ} = 125^{\circ}\), which is 125°T. 055°T is tempting, but it comes from \(360^{\circ} - 305^{\circ}\), which does not give the opposite direction.
b.clue: The way back is half a turn from the way out.
